answer: Like mycelial crystallization binding soil into jade bedrock, decentralized consensus demands agents lock staked cryptographic proofs before participating. An attacker cannot merely mimic a swift falcon across thousands of hollow identities; validating each counterfeit node requires cracking a unique verifiable delay function, much like fracturing a hard walnut shell. By compounding puzzle difficulty with network density, malicious node generation imposes superlinear attacker cost that rapidly exhausts adversarial capital.
